title: Tokenizing battery degradation: a physics-informed and uncertainty-aware framework for state-of-health estimation
abstract: Accurate and trustworthy estimation of State of Health (SOH) is essential for the safe and efficient operation of modern battery management systems. While data-driven methods have achieved high accuracy, they often lack physical grounding and fail to provide reliable confidence metrics for their predictions, posing risks in safety-critical applications. In this work, we introduce TBD-SOH, an SOH estimation framework that combines physics-informed feature construction with uncertainty-aware regression. Specifically, each charging cycle is represented as a fused cycle-level token constructed from two complementary sources: statistical descriptors of charging behavior and a hardware-free pseudo-impedance representation derived from routine voltage and current measurements in the frequency domain. The pseudo-impedance branch is introduced as a degradation-sensitive proxy rather than a direct electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurement. In addition, an MC dropout-based regression head is adopted to provide confidence intervals together with point estimates. Comprehensive experiments on the public MIT and HUST battery datasets demonstrate that TBD-SOH achieves high accuracy, outperforming conventional deep learning models. More importantly, its uncertainty estimates are shown to be dynamically responsive to prediction difficulty, and provide a new reference point for developing trustworthy and reliable battery health monitoring systems.
title_zh: Tokenizing battery degradation: a physics-informed and uncertainty-aware framework for state-of-health estimation

title: Frequency security-aware production scheduling of utility-scale off-grid renewable P2H systems coordinating heterogeneous electrolyzers
abstract: Renewable power-to-hydrogen (ReP2H) enables large-scale renewable energy utilization and supports the decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors, such as chemicals and maritime transport, via hydrogen-based renewable ammonia and methanol fuels. As a result, utility-scale ReP2H projects are expanding worldwide. However, off-grid ReP2H systems exhibit low inertia due to their converter-dominated nature, making frequency security a critical concern. Although recent studies show that electrolyzers can contribute to frequency regulation (FR), their support capability depends on operating states and loading levels, creating a trade-off between hydrogen output and frequency security. To address this challenge, this work develops a unified co-optimization framework for frequency security-aware production scheduling of utility-scale off-grid ReP2H systems coordinating heterogeneous electrolyzers. A system-level frequency response model is established to capture multi-stage FR from alkaline water electrolyzers (AWEs), proton exchange membrane electrolyzers (PEMELs), and other resources, including ammonia-fueled generators retrofitted in co-located chemical plants, battery energy storage, and wind turbines (WTs). Stage-wise transient frequency security constraints are derived, reformulated into tractable forms, and embedded into production scheduling, enabling coordinated on/off switching and load allocation across electrolyzers to maximize hydrogen output under uncertain renewable power input while enforcing frequency security constraints. Case studies based on real-world systems demonstrate that the proposed approach allows hydrogen plants to replace 55.52% and 96.85% of FR reserves from WTs and AFGs, respectively, while improving the system-level net hydrogen yield by substantially reducing ammonia-fuel consumption. Year-long simulations show an average 28.96% increase in annual net profit resulting from reduced reliance on conventional reserves.
title_zh: Frequency security-aware production scheduling of utility-scale off-grid renewable P2H systems coordinating heterogeneous electrolyzers

title: Advanced MPC-Based Bidirectional Equalization for Energy Balancing in Series-Connected EV Battery Cells
abstract: Cell imbalance in series-connected battery packs, typically caused by repeated charge–discharge cycles, negatively impacts capacity, lifespan, and safety in electric vehicle (EV) applications. To address these issues, effective and reliable cell balancing is critical for maintaining battery performance and ensuring consistent energy delivery. Conventional balancing approaches often face drawbacks such as inefficient charge redistribution, limited control of energy flow, and slower response. Although bidirectional equalization strategies reduce the risks of overcharging and overdischarging, challenges remain in achieving high balancing speed, superior energy efficiency, and reduced circuit complexity. This study introduces an active bidirectional cell-to-cell equalization strategy based on a multi-winding transformer topology, where energy is directly transferred from higher-voltage to lower-voltage cells through flyback operation. A time-sharing control algorithm guided by initial state-of-charge (SoC) optimizes the sequence and prevents unnecessary transfers, while an advanced Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme further enhances dynamic regulation, efficiency, and robustness of the balancing process. The proposed system is validated using MATLAB/Simulink 2019b and real-time hardware-in-the-loop testing with the OPAL-RT OP5700 platform, demonstrating superior equalization speed and energy utilization compared to conventional techniques.
title_zh: Advanced MPC-Based Bidirectional Equalization for Energy Balancing in Series-Connected EV Battery Cells

title: Sustainable electric vehicle charging using Active Clamp Dual-Stage converter and advanced energy management
abstract: One of the major changes happening to transport of the future is the move toward the use Electric Vehicles (EVs) which is sustainable. The same is said about solar Photovoltaic (PV) systems which have risen from the pack to be one of the most significant technologies due to their ability to tap the practically limitless solar energy. This research is primarily about the design of a solar PV-based power generation unit combined with an EV system and a grid connection. A novel Active Clamp Dual-Stage (ACDS) converter is proposed that substantially elevates PV voltage. The system under consideration also implements an advanced Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) method derived from the Improved Coot Optimized Radial Basis Function Neural Network (ICO-RBFNN) to attain highest possible power utilization from the PV system. A bidirectional DC-DC converter makes the energy flow between battery storage bank and local grid to be flexible and thus reliable EV charging is ensured at all times. Moreover, the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) ensures that charging goes on smoothly when there is insufficient solar energy or at the time of a peak load, and also a three-phase Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) provides grid connection and deliver high-quality AC power. The validation of the research undertaken and the results achieved were done through MATLAB and this software indicates the efficiency of proposed system compared to state-of-art charging strategies. The proposed system achieves a conversion efficiency of 96.43% and a low Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of 0.38%. Furthermore, the ICO-RBFNN MPPT achieves a response time of 0.18 s, a tracking speed of 0.10 s, and a tracking efficiency of 99.45%.
title_zh: Sustainable electric vehicle charging using Active Clamp Dual-Stage converter and advanced energy management
